candidate: C05 BOKU/Mendel/Masaryk in-house MS/MS library of flavonoids and prenylated flavonoids (Zenodo 16762591; Rypar et al., Metabolites 2025, 15, 616, PMC12471768)
method: metadata only; no spectra file read; no model run. Compound list = Table S1 of Supplementary Material File S3 (PMC12471768 zip, partial HTTP range reads). Exclusion sets and MURU key/scaffold definition from task P5.
reproduction: screen_c05_boku_flavonoid.py re-run 2026-09-15 (rdkit 2026.03.5): c05_screen_summary.json byte-identical to the 2026-09-14 run.
verdict_basis: Design A is excluded by verified, size-based facts that no further access can change: after MURU/PR7/comparator key and scaffold exclusion plus MassSpecGym 1.5 key exclusion the set is 17 compounds in 12 Bemis-Murcko groups (lenient variant 64 in 25 groups, 51.6% of keys in 3 groups). Criteria 5, 6 and 7 remain conditional on per-spectrum metadata that exists only inside in-house_MSMS_library.mgf (18.8 MB spectra file, outside this study's download policy).
open_items: K5 unresolved: the paper states HCD and CID energies 'in absolute values' (eV). Absolute HCD is vendor-supported on Tribrid 3.5 software, but the CID list includes 35, the canonical ion-trap normalized default, and the release note documents absolute/normalized for HCD only.
Zenodo names two instruments (Orbitrap IQ-X and Q Exactive HF); neither the paper's library section nor the metadata says which entries came from which instrument.
Per-compound adduct coverage ([M+H]+) is documented only as a general rule ('at least two adducts, most commonly protonated and deprotonated').

Authors report 47 of 64 prenylated compounds unique vs MSnLib, GNPS and MassSpecGym; this screen finds 42 of 64 absent from MassSpecGym 1.5 and the nine MSnLib libraries, i.e. more overlap, not less, despite covering fewer repositories.
